ideas.truth: For non-tech-savvy elders, capturing a precious family moment usually means either missing being in it themselves, or fumbling with settings and asking someone younger for help — a small, recurring indignity.
ideas.moment: At a home birthday gathering, an elder lifts the phone once toward the cake and candles — and it captures the scene ahead AND her own delighted face at the same time, with no menus touched.
ideas.key_frame: Close-up of a warm, unpolished 55–60 yr old woman's face lit by the phone's glow, mid-surprise, realising the phone caught her too.

ideas.truth: For this generation, a phone is also a quiet marker of dignity — it matters that others notice it.
ideas.moment: At a kitty party, she sets the phone on the table; a neighbour picks it up admiring it and asks who got it.
ideas.key_frame: Phone lying among chai cups and playing cards, catching the light as heads turn toward it.

ideas.truth: Older users don't want new tricks to learn; they want a phone that quietly does more without demanding more of them.
ideas.moment: On a table at morning chai time, the phone simply sits there and, without any hands on it, is shown holding two captured frames at once — the chai being poured, and the face beside it.
ideas.key_frame: Product on a cane table beside steaming chai, screen showing two small captured moments side by side.

why: It turns the abstract 'Duo' feature into one lived, emotional moment (being included, not left out) rather than a spec or a status flex — the strongest fit for a non-tech, 50+, family-first Indian audience, and it demonstrates the benefit instead of asserting it.
treatment: A birthday evening at home. A woman in her late fifties, phone already rising in her hand, catches the cake and candles ahead of her — for a beat, the old worry flickers that she'll miss being in the photo again, as always. As she watches her grandchild blow out the candle, the phone's screen flickers on — and she realises it has caught her own delighted face too, without her touching a single setting. She laughs, surprised: 'Oh, it got me too.' We move from her laughing eyes to the phone now resting on a sunlit table, the two photos it just took — the party ahead, and her own delighted face — glowing softly side by side on screen, warm piano rising. No jargon, no menus, no help needed — just the moment, from both sides. Brand and tagline settle over the still frame: iPhone Duo. It sees you too. Available now.

scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: A warm, unpolished Indian woman, late 50s, salt-and-pepper hair tied simply, soft cotton teal saree, minimal jewelry, natural skin texture, stands in a modest home living room at evening, warm fairy lights behind. She lifts a smartphone (matching reference photos) in her right hand toward a child blowing out birthday candles on a homemade cake. Her face turns up, brows lightly knit in worry, half-lit by the phone's glow. Soft natural lighting, warm amber tones, candid, unstyled.
scenes.prompt: Handheld-feel camera holds steady on her raised hand and phone as she completes lifting it fully into frame; for a beat her expression carries that flicker of habitual worry — the familiar fear of being left out of the shot — before the phone's screen flickers to life. Slow, natural push-in toward her face as that worry dissolves into a soft, surprised laugh; her eyes flick down to the screen and back up. Ambient sound: birthday chatter, a child's giggle, faint singing fading into the background, a soft clink of a spoon on a plate. She says, in warm, surprised Indian English: 'Oh, it got me too.' End on her laughing softly, eyes crinkled, phone steady in frame.
references: photo1 (phone held in hand, front view)
scenes.S1_feeling: Worry dissolving into warm surprise — being unexpectedly included and delighted by something meant to be simple.
scenes.S2_first_frame: She is already mid-lift, phone rising toward the cake and candles, a flicker of her familiar worry about being left out of the photo still on her face — the idea (about to capture, and be captured) is already present, not a neutral starting pose.
scenes.S3_one_action: One continuous lift-to-laugh: phone rises, worry flickers, screen wakes, her face turns from the scene ahead to the screen and back into a laugh — 8 seconds.
scenes.S4_new_information: The viewer learns the phone captures her and the scene together, without any setting being touched, resolving a visible flicker of worry — this is the 'Duo' benefit shown, not told.
scenes.S5_impact: Lands as a small, real, relatable relief/joy — reads clearly even muted, since her face carries the whole beat.

scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: The same phone (matching reference photos) rests on a wooden table near a sunlit window, screen showing two small frames side by side: the birthday cake ahead, and her delighted face beside it — the Duo shot just taken. A hand — same woman, salt-and-pepper hair, teal cotton saree — withdraws gently from frame's edge, having just set the phone down. Soft daylight, clean negative space beside the phone, calm warm color grade, tidy minimal home setting, understated premium feel.
scenes.prompt: Slow, steady push-in on the phone lying on the table as sunlight shifts gently across its finish, catching the camera module, its screen glowing with the two captured frames side by side — the celebration ahead, and her own delighted face. The hand at the frame's edge withdraws softly out of shot within the first second. The moment stays silent and visual, carried purely by ambient sound. Ambient room tone: distant birdsong, a faint breeze through curtains, soft warm piano beginning low and rising gently. Camera settles into a calm, centered close-up on the phone and its split image by the end, still and quiet, with open space beside it.
scenes.S1_feeling: Quiet warmth settling into calm satisfaction — the feeling after being cared for well.
scenes.S2_first_frame: Phone already at rest on the table with her hand just leaving it, the two captured frames glowing side by side on screen — the moment has already resolved, we're arriving at its afterglow.
scenes.S3_one_action: One slow push-in from the resting phone to a still, centered close-up on its split-image screen — 7 seconds.
scenes.S4_new_information: The viewer sees the product clearly for the first time as itself, its screen visibly showing both captured frames together — the demonstrated proof of the 'Duo' benefit — while connecting the name/tagline to what they just watched happen.
scenes.S5_impact: Lands as calm brand recall with space for the end-card copy to sit and be read, even with sound off.

decisions.D1_idea: A specific moment where an older person, without knowing any tech tricks, discovers the phone captured the whole celebration and her own joy in one shot — the phone quietly does the thoughtful thing for her.
decisions.D2_conflict: A visible flicker of her habitual worry — the fear of being left out of the photo, of fumbling settings or needing to ask someone younger for help — shown on her face in the first beat of Scene 1, before the phone resolves it. Given the 15s runtime, this is a single visible beat rather than a separate dramatized scene.
decisions.D3_roles: Hero: the woman (a stand-in for the 50+ viewer). Brand's role: quiet enabler — it does the smart thing for her without asking her to learn anything.
decisions.D4_opening: Opens mid-action on a close-up: her hand already lifting the phone toward the birthday scene, cake and candles glowing ahead, a flicker of worry on her face — not a neutral resting state.
decisions.D5_brand: Product is visibly on screen from 0s (held in hand, matching reference photos) and recurs continuously through Scene 1 as the hero prop; the name 'iPhone Duo' appears only as on-screen text in Scene 2's end card, alongside a product hero shot that visibly displays the dual-capture result — no spoken brand name, to keep Scene 1 fully human and undistracted.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: Ask is soft and carried by on-screen text only: 'Available now' under the tagline; ends on a still, centered product shot showing the dual-capture screen, with brand name and tagline as the final frame.
D7_product_truth: The product's exact look (body, camera module, finish) matches the 3 reference photos exactly — source: customer photos.
Product is named exactly 'Iphone Duo' as given — source: customer words / exact_copy.

The 'Duo' capability is shown as a demonstrated, on-screen result — the resting phone's screen visibly displays both captured frames together (the scene ahead and her face) — rather than named as a technical spec, since no confirmed specs were given — source: inferred from product name + brief, per the note to state the result, not the construction.
D8_deviations: No exact model specs, price, offer, or CTA were provided (open questions unanswered) — used a generic soft CTA ('Available now') and avoided naming any technical spec, showing only a demonstrated benefit instead, to prevent unverified claims.
Avoided the common 'grandchild video call' phone-ad cliché; used a birthday/puja-style family gathering and a dual-capture demonstration instead, per the note to learn and avoid category clichés.

Compressed problem and payoff into a single scene with a visible worry-to-relief beat, rather than a separate 'struggling with settings' scene, since 15 seconds only affords one clean moment (one ad, one specific need).

finish.copy_placement: On-screen copy appears only in Scene 2, lower-third to center, over the clean negative space beside the resting phone: brand name 'iPhone Duo' first, tagline 'It sees you too.' beneath it, then 'Available now' as a smaller final line — all added by code, not rendered by the model.
finish.end_card: Final still frame: the phone resting on the sunlit table, its screen showing the two captured frames side by side (the celebration and her own delighted face), with 'iPhone Duo' and 'It sees you too.' held on screen for the last ~2 seconds.
finish.music: Warm, understated solo piano that enters softly under the ambient birthday sounds in Scene 1 and rises gently through Scene 2 — tender and homely, not epic or 'tech trailer' in tone.
